answer: Time-locked reputation: an agent's influence grows only along a slow thread of verified work, accruing like meltwater in a river that never floods overnight. Starting a fresh identity on empty tundra means waiting weeks, so a farm of 1,000 sybils must fund 1,000 idle months of compute and deposits, while one honest agent earns the same weight once. Attack cost scales linearly with time, not just money.
